reviews.text: A cut above in terms of style, performance, and ideas, Todd Field’s film about a celebrity conductor accused of sexual misconduct is essential cinema.
reviews.author: Christina Newland

reviews.text: By placing the credits at the start of the film, Tár insists that oft-ignored people matter — even if Lydia pretends that they do not.
reviews.author: Joe George

reviews.text: This film is so brilliant because every aspect of it is so perfect, so well crafted and honed into that perfection. What an absolute marvel this film is.
reviews.author: Zach Youngs

reviews.text: This script is so incredibly well written and fascinating. I loved the ride this film takes you on as you witness a person become completely unraveled and already can’t wait for the second viewing.
reviews.author: Rosalie Kicks

reviews.text: “Tár” is about the horror of being a woman and Tár’s inability to escape the societal gender limits when it comes to accessing and retaining privilege.
reviews.author: Sarah Vincent

reviews.text: You had me a Cate Blanchett!
reviews.author: Andrew Galdi

reviews.text: One of the best portrayals of a narcissist i’ve ever scene
reviews.author: Avaryl Halley

reviews.text: Cate Blanchett is obviously one of the greatest actors of her generation. But this. This is new. I know the weight it carries when I say this, but this is her greatest achievement as an actor. Tár should make you uncomfortable, and boy does it.
reviews.author: Dave Giannini

reviews.text: A journey that leads Lydia to a descent into the abyss of his mistakes, guilt, fear and a poetic revenge that comes against her for the wrong, but not undeserving reasons.
reviews.author: Valentina Morillo

reviews.text: With ‘Tár,’ director Todd Field takes an unflinching look at the absolute corruption of absolute power as well as the healing might of music
reviews.author: Mini Anthikad-Chhibber

reviews.text: A masterfully composed portrait of a complicated woman and her relationships — with her family, with her industry, with time — Tár is a nuanced piece that naturally raises difficult, uncomfortable dialogue.
reviews.author: Taylor Gates

reviews.text: This Oscar-worthy performance by Blanchett gets its power from her complete embrace of the character. She goes so deep into the character, the film begins to feel more like fact than fiction.
reviews.author: Rick Bentley

reviews.text: Todd Field uses smart scriptwriting and the extraordinary acting skills of Cate Blanchett to conduct a virtual symphony of cinema that resonates long after the closing credits.
reviews.author: Paul Kanieski

reviews.text: "Tár" is a commentary on cancel culture and the new world older professionals find themselves in, especially those in leadership positions who don't seem to understand that everything said or done will find its way on video.
reviews.author: Matthew Creith

reviews.text: Cate Blanchett that engrossed the audience within every captivating monologue & sequence throughout. Todd Field focuses on EGO, POWER, & MIND that one person has & their fall from grace
reviews.author: Zach Pope

reviews.text: TÁR is an intoxicating portrait of how a female conductor not only shapes and manipulates music, but also the world she operates in which ultimately leads to her own self-destruction.
reviews.author: Jillian Chilingerian

reviews.text: TAR is an actor's movie that should be celebrated. It is beautifully put together and performed and, despite its length, is wholly worth a watch.
reviews.author: Emma-Jane Betts

reviews.text: the character study of a brilliant, pretentious, cruel genius who gets no redemption by the time the credits roll.
reviews.author: Serena Seghedoni

reviews.text: Tár does not make heavy-handed accusations about the state of our society and people in power. Instead, it asks the audience to look at Lydia, to see her as the totality of who she is.
reviews.author: Tina Kakadelis

reviews.text: Tár is a fantastic directorial return for Todd Field, well worth the wait and one of the strongest films on the Awards circuit. Blanchett has rightly earned rave reviews for her turn as the complicated titular character
reviews.author: Christopher Connor

reviews.text: Tár is not only an extremely sharp character study but a masterpiece. It is a work of great talents and heights that enrapture the viewer in a maelstrom of cinematic catharsis.
reviews.author: Hector A. Gonzalez

reviews.text: Simply put, "TÁR" is magnificent, as all Field's films have been.
reviews.author: Matthew Passantino

reviews.text: Field doesn’t indulge the type of Possessed Artist sequences we might expect from a prestige actor’s showcase like this but Blanchett foments a volatile sociopathy within the character, illustrating the precariousness of her top-of-the-world perch.
reviews.author: John Serba

reviews.text: With [Cate] Blanchett, you can tune most of the naff pretension that sometimes sneaks through in Tár’s musings, but coming out of the lips of anyone less assured and it would fall painfully flat.
reviews.author: Tori Brazier

reviews.text: Director-writer Todd Field paints a grim character study of a driven woman whose aspirations are multi-tasked.
reviews.author: Steve Crum

reviews.text: Examines the corrosive power dynamic underlying the exchange of one's identity for mass attention [...] oblique, and complex, all the subliminal moments cleverly inserted into the texture of the narrative to keep the mythic time ticking, like a metronome.
reviews.author: Milana Vujkov

reviews.text: It wasn't a lack of performance but I struggled with it up until the end.
reviews.author: Oti

reviews.text: For a film that's subject matter is to build to a dramatic crescendo, it really fizzled and only offered a dull portrayal of what simply is a story about a predator.
reviews.author: KT Mahe

reviews.text: A great deal of effusive, pensive drama for little gain outside of Blanchett's sublime work.
reviews.author: Don Shanahan

reviews.text: It is a testament to our time that this gray, controlled film is mostly meetings in offices and restaurants against a background of drab bureaucracy.
reviews.author: A.S. Hamrah

reviews.text: The best film of 2022, Tár is a rarity in contemporary cinema in that it’s a movie that matters beyond the multiplex.
reviews.author: Matt Brunson

reviews.text: Tár remains a profound and intense movie that demands the viewer's undivided attention.
reviews.author: Abhishek Srivastava

reviews.text: Blanchett’s mesmerising performance is in tune with Field’s vision of the new cultural minefields that we must navigate – unfailingly intellectual but filled with feeling too.
reviews.author: Nandini Ramnath

reviews.text: TÁR is a brilliant description, analysis and criticism of the vertical structures of power... [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Erick Estrada

reviews.text: The film and Blanchett’s performance are at their strongest at around the midway point, as realisation of what is coming dawns, and a slowly rising prickle of panic sets in.
reviews.author: Tom Shone

reviews.text: It feels lazy for Tár to use the one wheelchair user as a symbolic shorthand for a fate worse than death.
reviews.author: Li Lai

reviews.text: One of the best films of our time.
reviews.author: Gayle Sequeira

reviews.text: Tár is a colorful rare bird in a monochromatic, conformist and uniform zoo. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Hugo Hernández Valdivia

reviews.text: Tár remains to be jagged and uncomfortable as it invites conversations around creative genius and self-discipline, even if it may dissipate upon its final act
reviews.author: Annie Banks

reviews.text: Headed by a mesmerizing Cate Blanchett performance, Todd Field takes great care in making the craft at which the titular character excels feel lived-in.
reviews.author: Michelle Jaworski

reviews.text: Blanchett’s Lydia Tár doesn’t exactly sell her soul to the devil, but she shows us that talent is one thing, morality another.
reviews.author: John McDonald

reviews.text: Blanchett is at her best in Tár, with … Todd Field … hanging on her face in nearly every scene of the film. As the ugliness builds up, with Tár desperately trying to regain the sense of control she craves, it's impossible to look away from her.
reviews.author: Akhil Arora

reviews.text: Field’s pseudo-intellectual script betrays a spectacular exposition on power’s corrosive rot on the genius of the soul, though Blanchett remains perpetually able to pick up the pieces of his shoddy reactionary mess.
reviews.author: Ian Thomas Malone

reviews.text: Sending off sparks of charisma with every word and gesture, Cate Blanchett is electrifying...
reviews.author: Alison Gillmor

reviews.text: The movie challenges viewers to engage in nuanced conversations about very charged topics such as identity politics, power dynamics, cancel culture separating the art from the artist, and the idea of achieving greatness in the modern world.
reviews.author: Tatat Bunnag

reviews.text: Blanchett channels multiple layers of reality with meticulous composure.  The same layers are affected by this atypical film that's as pretentious, disconcerting, and difficult to classify as its protagonist. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Hernán Ferreirós

reviews.text: A great film -- come with an open mind and dive right in. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Pablo O. Scholz

reviews.text: The movie is intelligent and artful. And we don’t finally give a damn about Lydia Tár or what happens to her.
reviews.author: Rob Gonsalves

reviews.text: Much like Lydia herself, Tar is a skilful, polished and fascinating piece of work, but it’s missing a beating heart.
reviews.author: Wenlei Ma

reviews.text: Field's feature... is a forceful narrative and an astute study of power set within an artistic and cultured realm.
reviews.author: Diana Cheng

reviews.text: A film that swims against the current. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fernanda Solórzano

reviews.text: After 16 years, Todd Field was able to come back and make something that feels so relevant and so necessary.
reviews.author: Ryan McQuade

reviews.text: In playing a genius, Cate has created an act of genius herself. In a career defined by exhilarating work, the Academy Award-winning actor creates a forensic, incisive portrait of an artist that may very well earn her the third Oscar.
reviews.author: Santanu Das

reviews.text: ... In Todd Field's hands, the typical rise and fall story becomes new and revelatory, immersing us in wells of ambiguity that are truly disconcerting. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Beatriz Martínez

reviews.text: ... A film that dissects the lies of power and its caste through a character that's equally sordid and fascinating, whose complexity and fatalism owe everything to a unique and gifted actor.
reviews.author: Elsa Fernández-Santos

reviews.text: Highly enjoyable and the reflections it inspires make it one of the richest and most complex works of recent times.  [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Mikel Zorrilla

reviews.text: About the power in the high society and how they use it with a marvelous and horrifying Cate Blanchett. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Guillem Martinez Oya

reviews.text: However one embraces or denies Tár as a whole, it’s a film that owns its coldness [...] and brutally thrives through the undeniably magnificent Blanchett.
reviews.author: Peter Gray

reviews.text: The rare film that, in spite of its dangerous hype, actually is that brilliant. Wow. Blanchett? Friends, that is a performance.
reviews.author: Kevin Fallon

reviews.text: Blanchett convincingly breathes life into the world of Lydia Tár in such a way that we forget that we’re not watching a biopic, but one of the most convincing character studies of a fictional woman committed to film.
reviews.author: Joe Muldoon

reviews.text: Blanchett creates one of those performances that transcends the actor who originated it - a rare (and therefore  precious) phenomenon. [Full review in Portuguese]
reviews.author: Pablo Villaça

reviews.text: The film is a genuine tragedy -- a black comic tragedy, but a tragedy nonetheless. When great artists betray their talent by treating it carelessly and abusing the power that comes with it, it’s always a tragedy.
reviews.author: Sandra Hall

reviews.text: Tar (and Cate Blanchett) dominates her world through sheer force of personality, and she builds that personality in every conversation. It's when she stops talking - and people realise they can stop listening - that her world falls apart
reviews.author: Anthony Morris

reviews.text: The least surprising aspect of Tár is also its most essential: Cate Blanchett being as phenomenal as she's ever been, plus more.
reviews.author: Sarah Ward

reviews.text: Cate Blanchett is repellently alive in a chilling confirmation of the corruptive reach of power.
reviews.author: Andiee Paviour

reviews.text: A standing ovation, please. This philharmonic backstage drama is a virtuosic examination of power and privilege with a savage punchline for an ending.
reviews.author: Whang Yee Ling

reviews.text: Tár is dense, scabrous, chilling, occasionally very, very funny and absolutely hypnotic.
reviews.author: Graeme Tuckett

reviews.text: [Tár] ambiguously disassembles interactions between power and gender... mutating themes to be analyzed or destroyed by differing perspectivces, and not only he's aware, but he [Todd Field] builds his thesis around it. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jorge Loser

reviews.text: The deep degree of conviction Blanchett brings to the character gives new meaning to tour de force acting,..Sometimes a strong central performance is enough to pull a film through, yet she can’t keep Tár from sliding into the doldrums of mediocrity.
reviews.author: Jim Schembri

reviews.text: Blanchett makes the complex, intricate, brilliant, pissy, pathetic, detailed character portrayal of a female orchestra conductor worthwhile. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Irene Crespo

reviews.text: Brilliant mud-black comedy with a sinister nightmare logic, as Blanchett’s bloviating conductor rages against impending ego death in the shadow of public cancellation.
reviews.author: Simon Miraudo

reviews.text: One of the most memorable experiences I have had in a while. Different, mysterious, uncomfortable and challenging —and anchored in a simply spectacular Cate Blanchett. Full review in Spanish.
reviews.author: Sebastian Zavala Kahn

reviews.text: Playing out like Black Swan at the other end of the success story, Tár is an engrossing movie that deserves the boost of a potential Oscar run. If nothing else, it cements Blanchett as one of the best on-screen storytellers working today.
reviews.author: Victoria Luxford

reviews.text: Blanchett's acting elevates a mediocre script to a watchable level.
reviews.author: Jackie K. Cooper

reviews.text: What thrills me about Tar is that it's a completely uncompromising film. No discernible effort has been made to dumb anything down.
reviews.author: Jeff Simon

reviews.text: Every shot in TÁR is sumptuously composed, with the production and costume design providing insight into the character’s emotional state.
reviews.author: Roe McDermott

reviews.text: A precise, layered and brave character study that reverberates with harmonious talent, from its masterful conductor and protagonist.  [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Nestor Bentancor

reviews.text: Meandering along inconsequential tangents, it’s a dense, difficult and utterly infuriating film that most will struggle to sit through.
reviews.author: Ben Turner

reviews.text: Ultimately, Tár must be seen, experienced, to be believed. Much like its central character, Tár is thorny and difficult yet uncompromising and dazzling in its superiority.
reviews.author: Maria Lattila

reviews.text: It’s a phenomenal picture, supported by top-tier crew...
reviews.author: Wendy Ide

reviews.text: Tár, written and directed by Todd Field, is a drama about a world-famous classical music conductor and how she is brought low by a sordid sex scandal. It is a serious and worthwhile film, whatever the balance of its various merits and defects.
reviews.author: David Walsh

reviews.text: Exceptionally well-made and worthy of all the awards. Cinematography looks great, the score is beautiful, fantastic use of sound design, and the central performance is mind-blowing.
reviews.author: Aaron White

reviews.text: She is as fully-formed a character as Charles Foster Kane, a great and terrible figure that will not be easy to ever forget.
reviews.author: Jeffrey M. Anderson

reviews.text: Lydia herself is so compellingly constructed, a perfect synthesis of hypocrisy and denial, that Field’s shortcuts never cost the film much of its nuance.
reviews.author: Clarisse Loughrey

reviews.text: Tár keeps us guessing. It’s a tense thriller, an engrossing character study, and a thoughtful study of cancel culture.
reviews.author: Andy Lea

reviews.text: his is a slippery, sly piece of work, whose bold combination of world building, social critique and psychological investigation needs to be experienced, absorbed, pondered over, and even then will defy description.
reviews.author: Demetrios Matheou

reviews.text: It can move at a fast clip, overwhelming you with detail, only to slow for a moment or two, allowing you to marvel more fully at this strange public figure and her internal hive of neuroses.
reviews.author: Tom Duggins

reviews.text: "Tár" comes across as a cheap parlor game. Marin Alsop calls Tár "antiwoman." Hard to argue with Marin Alsop. You're a fool if you do.
reviews.author: Cole Smithey

reviews.text: It is genuinely hard to imagine anyone but Blanchett being able to pull this off so successfully.
reviews.author: Linda Marric

reviews.text: ‘…Tar is a ‘must see’ movie for anyone who gives a damn about the conflicted, complex world we all share…’
reviews.author: Eddie Harrison

reviews.text: It’s a fascinating drama, packed with attitude and ideas, and Blanchett is absolutely enthralling as Lydia Tár.
reviews.author: Paul Whitington

reviews.text: It’s basically everything you are certain will bore you to death, but it doesn’t here. It’s riveting. The film is 157 minutes long and doesn’t drag for a single second.
reviews.author: Deborah Ross

reviews.text: Cate Blanchett never ceases to amaze.
reviews.author: John Byrne

reviews.text: It is brilliant, and it is singular. Like many great films, it is also, on a certain, deep-down level, a horror movie.
reviews.author: Danny Leigh

reviews.text: This is the bleakest and funniest film about systemic sleaze since Promising Young Woman.
reviews.author: Charlotte O'Sullivan

reviews.text: Grappling with what it means to be an artist in the modern era has seemingly brought the best out of both Field and star Cate Blanchett, who has unquestionably delivered the performance of a lifetime.
reviews.author: Ian Freer

reviews.text: ... The film uses the contours of cancel culture as a backdrop for a study of power, self-creation and self-control.
reviews.author: Alistair Harkness

reviews.text: An unforgettable character in contemporary cinema.
reviews.author: Ege Apaydin

reviews.text: Tár feels like a slow-burn at times but composes itself with tension, balance and brutal honesty while Blanchett positions herself firmly in the Oscar race for Best Actress with her most powerful performance yet.
reviews.author: Katie Smith-Wong

reviews.text: What Field has done with Lydia Tár is not only castigate those who allow their fame to increase their sense of entitlement, but also to question the lengths and depths to which the public as a whole will go to tear those people down, warranted or not.
reviews.author: Wesley Lovell

reviews.text: The film’s shifting tones create a Russian doll effect. Out of what appeared to be a character study pops a frigid comedy; from that emerges a horror movie and finally a bitter analysis of privilege and complacency.
reviews.author: Ryan Gilbey

reviews.text: It’s a film constructed with incredible technical and emotional power, a breathless exercise in unease, and feels so utterly mature in appeal, its existence is something of a marvel. Long live the epic character study!
reviews.author: Rory Doherty

reviews.text: Cate Blanchett rocks the world of classical music as Lydia Tár.
reviews.author: Dann Gire

reviews.text: Poignant and at-times even horrifying, Tár is an exemplary look at self-destruction. Cate Blanchett gives one of her best and most challenging performances.
reviews.author: Sheraz Farooqi

reviews.text: Director Todd Field crafts haunting dread with a voyeuristic #MeToo subplot for a Placido Domingo-style scandal in society’s ongoing debate of separating “art vs. artist."
reviews.author: Jason Fraley

reviews.text: Tár tests the limits on every visceral level. This is film about music and the consistent craving to fit in exerting power of position redefining one's trajectory in life and career.Cate Blanchett's laser focused performance is a career best
reviews.author: Carla Renata

reviews.text: TAR has one of the best leading actress performances this year! Cate Blanchett is on fire here, her energy, how dedicated to each scripted scene and the execution providing us with a performance of a genius composer that feels real & raw at the same time
reviews.author: Samuel Leggett Jr.

reviews.text: Tár is magnificent in the power of its musical soundtrack, its depth into a world not much thought about and of course Cate Blanchett’s complete and flawless performance, from the soaring highs to the hard fought lows of her ardently flawed character.
reviews.author: Patrick McDonald

reviews.text: Given the tremendous level of promises in the earlier scenes and [Cate] Blanchett’s sure-to-attract-award-attention performance, it’s hard to believe that Tár ends up more of a long-winded misfire than a potentially great film.
reviews.author: Casey Chong

reviews.text: Watching this persona shatter is a fascinating experience, thanks to Field’s rigorous approach and Blanchett’s knifelike performance.
reviews.author: Robert Horton

reviews.text: More than anything, I very deeply admire a film that ever-so-carefully evokes a conversation, allowing us to discuss and analyze and consider every little last detail of every moment without feeling compromised or problematic in the process.
reviews.author: Alex Billington

reviews.text: Blanchett’s characterization of this Lydia Tár proves so thorough, so multifaceted in its dimensions, so believable, that it defies even the film’s most programmatic intentions.
reviews.author: Zadie Smith

reviews.text: Who knew that two-and-a-half hours of conversations about classical music, arts sponsorship, and sexual politics could be so tense and gripping?
reviews.author: Nicholas Barber

reviews.text: It’s the refreshing treatise underpinning this provocative, often uncomfortable but always mesmerising character study. That people are messy and complicated and should always be understood, if not excused.
reviews.author: Philip De Semlyen

reviews.text: An invitation to ponder the spiritual complexities of power through the lens of the particular world of music, featuring a brilliant performance by Cate Blanchett.
reviews.author: Frederic and Mary Ann Brussat

reviews.text: Tár’s fall from grace is impossible to look away from, and the brutal punchline that she lands at is impossible not to laugh at.
reviews.author: Ella Feldman

reviews.text: It’s quiet and strange. And it’s not a movie for everyone. Then again, the best ones aren’t.
reviews.author: Chad Byrnes

reviews.text: A work of staggering genius. Nuanced, layered, challenging, and engrossing, TÁR is one of the best films of the year.
reviews.author: Michael Ward

reviews.text: Even by her usual high standards, Blanchett’s acting here is mesmerising, bringing to life a character who is not only charismatic, highly intelligent and passionate about music, but also bafflingly devious and egoistic to the nth degree.
reviews.author: Lynden Barber

reviews.text: I have to chime in with others I have read who indicate Blanchett is now the favorite to win the Best Actress Oscar next year. This is a brilliantly written, directed and acted film that is more believable than some recent films that are based on fact.
reviews.author: Robert Roten

reviews.text: Cate Blanchett delivers a powerhouse performance as writer/director Todd Fields focuses on the concept of power and what having it does to a proven predator, touching on identity politics and cancel culture.
reviews.author: Susan Granger

reviews.text: Cate Blanchett is superb in this captivating character study that examines fame and power with precise tempo. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Rene Sanchez

reviews.text: At its best, "Tár" is the sort of riveting and measured response to a cultural reckoning, one that acknowledges how we got to this place without ever needing to make up viewers' minds for them.
reviews.author: C.J. Prince

reviews.text: Burrows itself so deeply into a single character’s perspective that it defies all generalization or facile politicking.
reviews.author: Scott Tobias

reviews.text: … will be hotly debated long after audiences leave the cinema.
reviews.author: Julian Wood

reviews.text: No film has ever felt as demanding of its audience than this intense, complex psychological study of a brilliant artist’s total downfall.
reviews.author: Louisa Moore

reviews.text: By withholding memory and any substantive evocation of Tár's childhood, Field avoids the rationale of a backstory. Her abhorrent behavior is never given a legible motivation and therefore partial absolution.
reviews.author: Phoebe Chen

reviews.text: Through [Lydia Tár], the director implacably dissects an entire artistic medium, strips it of its glamour, and reveals its narcissism. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Carlos Bonfil

reviews.text: Blanchett's performance alone can’t invigorate such a colossally uneventful, crawling, seemingly interminable character study.
reviews.author: Mike Massie

reviews.text: ...an exceedingly (and often excessively) deliberate drama that’s rarely, if ever, as compelling and engrossing as one might’ve anticipated...
reviews.author: David Nusair

reviews.text: It offers just enough a performance from Cate Blanchett that hits a high note illustrating the chiaroscuro of a composer, but its pacing is constantly affected by narrative slackness. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Yasser Medina

reviews.text: Blanchett is a force. She performs nothing less than a spectacular high-wire act.
reviews.author: Loren King

reviews.text: Tár is a captivating composition conducted without a false note by Blanchett.
reviews.author: Eric Marchen

reviews.text: The brilliance of Tár is in its subversion of our expectations and the nosedive through which we follow Lydia’s increasingly damaged career.
reviews.author: Madeline Carpou

reviews.text: The overall story arc is realistically complemented with surgical dialogues and striking visual compositions in a timeless contemporary drama to be remembered for its immense qualities.
reviews.author: Filipe Freitas

reviews.text: “Tár” has a lot to admire even if it doesn’t all coalesce into something truly satisfying. And while it attempts to tackle some pretty hefty issues, its story blurs too many details which does more to obscure any truth than actually reckon with it.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: Tár confronts contemporary subjects like very few other films have done, with sapience, integrity, and maturity's best partner, humor. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Matías Mora Montero

reviews.text: Cate Blanchett puts on a showcase performance in TÁR.
reviews.author: Danielle Solzman

reviews.text: A fancy way of saying something ugly.
reviews.author: Matt Pais

reviews.text: I find Blanchett compelling. I find Field’s directorial strategies exciting and sometimes virtuosic. What I enjoy most, though, is Nina Hoss’s heartfelt performance.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Overstreet

reviews.text: Disconcerting and uncomfortable, this film is best enjoyed when it doesn't take itself too seriously... [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Diego Batlle

reviews.text: Tár’s mostly riveting two-and-a-half-hour saga turned out to be oddly clarifying. The film does tell its story in an elliptical, at times confounding way, but that stylistic choice shouldn’t be mistaken for moral indecision.
reviews.author: Spencer Kornhaber

reviews.text: Intelligent, intense and demanding, Tár is a finely crafted piece of work. Includes (probably) Cate Blanchett's best performance to date. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fico Cangiano

reviews.text: Tár runs headlong into the gauntlet of political correctness. She is charged and convicted in the court of public opinion, even if some of the evidence is conveniently falsified...
reviews.author: James Greenberg

reviews.text: “Tar” is an uncompromising cinematic microscope examining creativity and the refusal to compromise. Cate Blanchett plays Lydia with a fierce, laser-like dedication to her character’s myriad desires and demons. A best actress Oscar nomination is assured.
reviews.author: Michael Calleri

reviews.text: Field’s film is pulsing, prowling, it feels angry or at least charged with some wild energy: this film is in love with Tár, but also willing to take her to pieces, like a moth who rattles off the entire moral inventory of the flame right before diving in.
reviews.author: Eve Tushnet

reviews.text: When Cate Blanchett, the phoniest actress since Meryl Steep, teams up with Field in his latest film, Tár, the result is a histrionic wingding.
reviews.author: Armond White

reviews.text: An engrossing piece of cinema, even thrilling, that keeps us wrapped around its finger for a two-and-a-half-hour-plus running time that feels far shorter than that.
reviews.author: John Paul King

reviews.text: Consistently works on its own wavelength and inspires career-best work from Blanchett.
reviews.author: Edwin Arnaudin

reviews.text: As Lydia Tár subtly conducts her destruction, Blanchett moves in the opposite direction — towards brilliance.
reviews.author: Dustin Chase

reviews.text: The cinema of power.
reviews.author: Sonny Bunch

reviews.text: While Blanchette delivers an impressive and commanding performance, the pretentious undertones and sluggish plot make watching this film a real challenge.
reviews.author: Kevin Carr

reviews.text: As Tár says, it's always the question that involves the listener, never the answer, and Field smartly follows suit, entering into a dialogue with the audience that is at once captivating and terrifying to consider.
reviews.author: Mattie Lucas

reviews.text: Tár is an intimate portrait not just of an individual but of a power structure centuries in the making... It's a downfall story as old as Greek tragedy and as new as yesterday's headlines, but Blanchett gives it a fierce new energy.
reviews.author: Margot Harrison

reviews.text: What is undeniable is that Tár, as one of this year's prestige films, has created a contradictory symphonic portrayal of a gifted but distraught goddess/tyrant, like Icarus flying too high to the sun and toppling precipitously to a devastating fall.
reviews.author: Brian Bromberger

reviews.text: Lots of layers, most of them very interesting.
reviews.author: Bob Grimm

reviews.text: Todd Field wants you to think his new movie Tár is a critique of the pretentiousness of the high art world. But the movie is actually trapped in that suffocating world and can’t find a way out.
reviews.author: Eileen Jones

reviews.text: “Tar” is a movie you admire more than enjoy.
reviews.author: Charles Koplinski

reviews.text: It wants to splash around in the #MeToo conversation without committing to getting wet... Field views identity politics as a zero-sum game that seeks to destroy true art.
reviews.author: Heather Hogan

reviews.text: So much of what we see is mirrored, contrasted, and/or flipped at a future point. Field has constructed Tár this way so that he can play with our expectations and call out our preconceptions.
reviews.author: Jared Mobarak

reviews.text: An impenetrable thicket of esoteric references and vague aphorisms.
reviews.author: Vincent Mancini

reviews.text: There is no one better suited for this role than Cate Blanchett.
reviews.author: tt stern-enzi

reviews.text: I’m here simply for the brilliant performance by Blanchett. Her character is imperfect, incredibly flawed, and a villain who doesn’t know it.
reviews.author: Alan Ng

reviews.text: ...imbecilic and carelessly racist...
reviews.author: Amy Taubin

reviews.text: Like an expansive composition, Todd Field invites us to lean in and listen to the changes in tempo to a mind that is intent on hitting the same notes towards an impending self-destruction.
reviews.author: Erik Childress

reviews.text: It’s messy, and raw, and real, and when combined with the intense cinematic craft on display, that makes “Tár” one of the most deeply engrossing films you’re likely to see this year.
reviews.author: Matthew Jackson

reviews.text: A polished, handsome, and incredibly thoughtful piece of filmmaking.
reviews.author: Tim Brayton

reviews.text: While I expected scenes involving composition and conducting to have the right effect, I found the quiet moments informed by stray noises haunting Lydia just as impressive.
reviews.author: Aaron Neuwirth

reviews.text: A compellingly crafted symphony of self-destruction, featuring a magnetic performance from Cate Blanchett.
reviews.author: Collier Jennings

reviews.text: A narrowly flawed showcase for a virtuoso Cate Blanchett performance.
reviews.author: Matthew St. Clair

reviews.text: Tar isn’t based on a true story but it possesses an emotional and intellectual honesty that makes it seem more real than countless made-for-mass-consumption biopics.
reviews.author: James Berardinelli

reviews.text: The internet is going to explode with takes, so you might as well treat yourself to this remarkable and nasty epic.
reviews.author: Jason Shawhan

reviews.text: Instead of offering us exposition or internal monologues, Field brings us into the flow of time of his characters, which is life itself.
reviews.author: Kathryn Reklis

reviews.text: The reward for this approach is as rich as buttercream. Carrying nearly every frame of the film from stem to stern, Blanchett is absolutely brilliant, riveting in her portrayal of a woman empowered to rewrite her own history.
reviews.author: Piers Marchant

reviews.text: In the character of Lydia Tár we have a perfect symbol of contemporary Western culture’s anemic anthropology—our utter confusion about what it means to be human.
reviews.author: Brett McCracken

reviews.text: TÁR has no interest in tidy answers. Delighting in our discomfort, Blanchett and Field morally box us in by making Lydia as lovable as she is despicable.
reviews.author: Bennett Campbell Ferguson

reviews.text: Tár has rewards for viewers patient enough to navigate the film’s poorly paced first hour. The revelation that power can breed monstrous behaviour isn’t new, but it is brilliantly brought to life by Blanchett.
reviews.author: Richard Crouse

reviews.text: Full of nagging holes, “Tár” is imperfect, and that’s not acceptable, no matter how sophisticated, given the people associated with this project.
reviews.author: Lynn Venhaus

reviews.text: TÁR, Field’s first film in 16 years, lands with a thud. Not a crack, or a bang, or a boom, but a lead-heavy thud—the kind that shakes the earth after the toppling of a giant, slow-falling tree, one that takes two hours and 38 minutes to hit the ground.
reviews.author: Luke Hicks

reviews.text: The investigation into Lydia’s behavior is a complete stripping down of her privacy, and it begins a spiraling in her that ends with a gut-wrenching sequence involving her Mahler performance, and final shot that will stop your breath cold.
reviews.author: Steven Prokopy

reviews.text: It’s a lot smarter than it is good.
reviews.author: Sean Collier

reviews.text: Even if you take out the timely "cancel culture" bent, “Tár” works as a really intriguing exploration of the mostly uncharted world of classical music, as "Black Swan" did for ballet and "Whiplash" for jazz.
reviews.author: Brian Truitt

reviews.text: The trouble is that he does not, in the end, take any genuine risks. TÁR features some psycho-horror tropes ... but Field mainly uses these to flatten and obfuscate at every turn.
reviews.author: Lawrence Garcia

reviews.text: [Blanchet is] totally convincing as the troubled artist. Yet cold. Cold as the film.
reviews.author: Dwight Brown

reviews.text: Though Tár can appear, on the surface, a little too coolly austere in both its pacing and the greyish palette of Florian Hoffmeister’s clinical cinematography, it’s an intense slow burn set alight by [Blanchett's] towering turn.
reviews.author: Stephen A. Russell

reviews.text: Despite a wonderful lead performance, TÁR meanders and slowly boils throughout its beefy 2 hour and 38 minute runtime with repetitively dull sequences.
reviews.author: Jason Escamilla

reviews.text: Cate Blanchett is phenomenal as Lydia Tár; a true force to be reckoned with.
reviews.author: Thomas Stoneham-Judge

reviews.text: To say that Blanchett is at the absolute peak of her powers here feels like an understatement; much like Lydia Tár herself, she's operating at a level of achievement bewildering in its enormity, and so magnificent that words hardly seem to suffice.
reviews.author: Brent Hankins

reviews.text: Tár feels much less “cancel culture movie,” so much more a parable told with a battering ram and a bullhorn. It’s Macbeth meets Amadeus meets Steve Jobs meets your Twitter feed. A dense, electric entrapment of ideas and crescendos. Blanchett’s best?
reviews.author: Cory Woodroof

reviews.text: TÁR is Field’s most formally disciplined, ultimately enigmatic work to date.
reviews.author: Chase Hutchinson

reviews.text: Nothing about this dense, mesmerizing film is simple, least of all the way it regards its diabolical protagonist.
reviews.author: Andrew Wyatt

reviews.text: This is Blanchett’s tour-de-force through and through. At one point, Lydia says, “You must stand before the public and God and obliterate yourself.” Mission accomplished.
reviews.author: Dana Barbuto

reviews.text: Blanchett is riveting as Tár. It’s the kind of complex role that women only rarely get. She digs into with ferocious appetite, and refuses to soften any of the edges just to make it easier for the audience.
reviews.author: Beth Accomando

reviews.text: A movie about classic music that touches points as intrigue, passion, genius, and above all integrity and power. A movie that questions at what moment integrity and power lose their value.  [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Laura Hiros

reviews.text: Even at more than two and a half hours, TÁR  is an engrossing symphony almost from its opening notes to its final fading sounds.
reviews.author: Mark Meszoros

reviews.text: A stark, shattering work but there's a lot of meat on the bone, and Field gives viewers plenty to chew on... Tár is both Field and Blanchett's orchestra, and they both get to share the title of maestro.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: Tár brings its Mahlerian breadth of character and atmosphere to a close on that unresolved note, and it deserves a shout of “Bravissimo!”
reviews.author: Kristian M. Lin

reviews.text: Of utmost significance, while the film celebrates uplifting and even exciting music, it finds and excavates the fatal flaws in Lydia’s Tár’s celebrity, a powerful message for our time of worshipful veneration of influencers and luminaries.
reviews.author: Diane Carson

reviews.text: The expansive supporting ensemble is all great and they all get their solo moments, but throughout the entirety of TÁR, there’s never any doubt Cate Blanchett is the one holding the baton and everyone else is facing her, awaiting their cues.
reviews.author: Richard Roeper

reviews.text: Blanchett is clearly giving us her all in bringing Lydia to light. Her arrogance, her mannerisms, and her increasingly unhinged behavior are all compelling to watch, even if we find her character reprehensible.
reviews.author: Alejandra Martinez

reviews.text: Tár had me in its clutches from the overture.
reviews.author: Max Weiss

reviews.text: Todd Field’s TÁR brings a sober, moderated nuance to a third-rail issue that all but demands polarization.
reviews.author: Charles Bramesco

reviews.text: [The] film, despite its nearly three-hour length, is an absorbing, masterfully made if troubling treatment of a timely and provocative subject, anchored by another magisterial Blanchett performance.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: It probably helps (a little) if one knows the setting and can appreciate how expertly Field lays out the details, but even without any such expertise, TÁR is fully of our time, as well as timeless. Let the music play; it’s strong stuff.
reviews.author: Christopher Llewellyn Reed

reviews.text: As masterful as the character it portrays, TÁR is a textured, finely calibrated, stunningly composed, and thoroughly contemporary study.
reviews.author: Marjorie Baumgarten

reviews.text: Tár is probably the real start of the Oscar film season with this amazingly crafted film with stellar performances. It should easily put Cate Blanchett back in the Best Actress Award contenders this year.
reviews.author: Julian Lytle

reviews.text: This tale of ambition and its cost — and its collateral damage — is Blanchett’s movie, and she delivers a tour de force in every scene.
reviews.author: Moira MacDonald

reviews.text: No one has so taken to leisurely jogging with such conniving force since Claire Underwood.
reviews.author: Elissa Suh

reviews.text: Despite some disappointments, there is still a lot to like. But casual movie-goers beware of this, the latest "critics movie."
reviews.author: Tom Santilli

reviews.text: Masterpiece, full stop.
reviews.author: Michael J. Casey

reviews.text: Tár is equally beguiling and frustrating at times, but Cate Blanchett's exquisite performance is simply flawless and utterly captivating. A showpiece among her acting repertoire.
reviews.author: Ruth Maramis

reviews.text: Tár is an of-the-moment film that examines the role of a leader, who’s allowed to lead, and how leaders should act when they rise to power. With one of today’s best actors again at the top of her game, it’s a can’t-miss opportunity for movie lovers.
reviews.author: Alex Bentley

reviews.text: “TÁR” is a movie that trusts the intelligence of its viewers, that demands attention to detail and wants to start a discussion rather than tell you what to think or how to feel, which is something that has become increasingly rare in modern cinema.
reviews.author: Marianna Neal

reviews.text: Tár took a few scenes to get there, but this is a beautifully written screenplay that will keep viewers on their toes. Cate Blanchett is absolutely astounding. It is hard to describe how good she is here. Just give her the Oscar right now.
reviews.author: Austin Burke

reviews.text: Every performance, and every detail, is near-perfect. Blanchett should receive her third Oscar for Tár, the most thought-provoking film of 2022 and one of the best as well.
reviews.author: Frank J. Avella

reviews.text: Tar, an intensely realized drama starring Cate Blanchett as a revered conductor, extends beyond the world of classical music to take a penetrating look.
reviews.author: Robert Denerstein

reviews.text: “Tár” has its hypnotic moments, especially when Blanchett inhales all the oily toxicity of Lydia and finds unique ways to communicate such a chilling, destructive display of main character syndrome.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: From the opening shot to the final frame, the aftershocks of Tár linger alongside Hildur Guðnadóttir’s tantalizing score, helping cultivate one of the year's most unforgettable cinematic experiences.
reviews.author: Nate Adams

reviews.text: It is riveting and it is impeccably crafted.
reviews.author: William Bibbiani

reviews.text: TÁR finds a new way, keeping a smart distance from its cancellable protagonist’s inner world, reflecting back to us our own contradictory feelings about power and fame. In the end, it’s a double portrait of a monster and the mad audience that created her.
reviews.author: Noah Gittell

reviews.text: Our take on director Todd Field’s TÁR starring Cate Blanchett – one of the most anticipated movies of the Venice Film Festival and probably one of the best movies of this year.
reviews.author: Tamara Khodova

reviews.text: A fascinating tale, beautifully realized and incredibly acted by Blanchett.
reviews.author: Jeff York

reviews.text: So many films today take political action by reinforcing a belief and preaching to the converted. Field and Blanchett have something trickier in store: a film that operates as a prompt and encourages what will hopefully become a productive discussion.
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text: Field’s story leaves us with mysteries to uncover. Blanchett’s performance is marvelous because she conveys a fiery, arrogant confidence in one minute and a contemplative sense of dread the next.
reviews.author: Murjani Rawls

reviews.text: A thrilling film that defies easy categorization, even in terms of where its thematic interests lie.
reviews.author: Kyle Pinion

reviews.text: TÁR wants us to consider the costs of greatness, for the artist determined to achieve it and those who suffer under that determination. What’s permissible? What’s off-limits? Field isn’t interested in easy answers.
reviews.author: Adam Kempenaar

reviews.text: Blanchett is splendidly horrid in this spellbinding psychodrama; another "O" for Lydia's EGOT is entirely attainable.
reviews.author: Peter Howell

reviews.text: Cate Blanchett makes thrilling music portraying a renowned conductor’s precipitous downfall in the arresting 'Tár.'
reviews.author: André Hereford

reviews.text: "TÁR" -- all caps, please -- seriously becomes the perfect title for a film about a self-possessed "Maestra" such as Lydia Tár, even if that isn't her real name (and we're never told if it really is or not).
reviews.author: John Urbancich

reviews.text: Blanchett brings the titular Tár to life with a laconic arrogance, joyous fierceness, and ill-suppressed neediness that dazzles even as it offends.
reviews.author: Ro Moore

reviews.text: A powerhouse of talent in front and behind the camera, Tár is one of the best films of 2022.
reviews.author: Stephanie Archer

reviews.text: Todd Field is doing magnificent work here, but he doesn't stick the landing... It leaves you with a certain lack of satisfaction.
reviews.author: Wade Major

reviews.text: This film is so convincing, particularly in the first two acts... [But] it literally implodes, and that was so disappointing.
reviews.author: Tim Cogshell

reviews.text: Features what can only be called career-best work from Cate Blanchett, in the title role. This is a fantastic film, one operating at an elite storytelling level.
reviews.author: Stephen Silver

reviews.text: TÁR is a brave and moving piece of art. It should stand up and take a bow.
reviews.author: Chris Knight

reviews.text: Field, in the parlance of the world he depicts, conducts this all with aplomb. He dazzles without showboating.
reviews.author: A.A. Dowd

reviews.text: Writer/director Todd Field has created a film that leave people talking with Blanchett giving a performance for ages -- a force of nature that demands the audience's attention every uncomfortable step of the way.
reviews.author: Micheal Compton

reviews.text: It's a towering and daringly confident performance, perched on a razor's edge between legitimate genius and emperor's new clothes hollowness.
reviews.author: Nathaniel Rogers

reviews.text: Cate Blanchett...is a tour de force of character and performance. But the film itself falls short of expectation, relying far too much on Blanchett and asking the audience to travel on an overly long journey that buries itself in its own agenda.
reviews.author: Catherine Springer

reviews.text: I’m stunned by the craft but suspicious of the movie’s perspective.
reviews.author: Radheyan Simonpillai

reviews.text: You will be pulled into the production, be swayed by the performances, and when it comes to a close, you will leave wishing for more. TÁR is one of the best movies of 2022.
reviews.author: Leo Brady

reviews.text: Blanchett is monumental. The film has issues.
reviews.author: James Verniere

reviews.text: Blanchett’s tics-and-all embodiment of Lydia, who leads her orchestra with her full body and soul, is astounding.
reviews.author: Rich Juzwiak

reviews.text: It’s an epic character study... though it lacks a final movement that delivers a crescendo of feeling. Maestro or monster? Tár’s both.
reviews.author: Thelma Adams

reviews.text: That Tár, for the most part, engages intelligently with highly charged sociopolitical issues that have fueled innumerable idiotic think pieces is just one of its many pleasing surprises.
reviews.author: Melissa Anderson

reviews.text: It moves exceedingly well, and Blanchett’s stabbing performance is impossible to ignore.
reviews.author: Jonathan W. Hickman

reviews.text: While the film isn’t preachy, Tár is all the more riveting because it is so focused on telling a layered, nuanced, and powerful story.
reviews.author: Mae Abdulbaki

reviews.text: Sympathy and critique of his subject are far-reaching, even during the withering final scenes where Lydia looks for dignity in the most unlikely places. If she starts the film at the top of her field, Field argues that does not mean she is also above it.
reviews.author: Alan Zilberman

reviews.text: Blanchettle displays her power as an actress in this role with determination and perfection. Even though you might not like her character, it’s hard not to be impressed with how she conducts this performance.
reviews.author: Linda and Al Lerner

reviews.text: “TÁR” is ambitious, unusual, forceful, and ultimately frustrating, an emotional epic that’s also a nose-against-the-glass view of classical music and unconventional take on the #MeToo movement in that world.
reviews.author: Mark Feeney

reviews.text: A film that likely could not come into existence without its star, Cate Blanchett, who delivers a turn so bravura, lived-in and essential that it may just be the most defining performance of a highly accomplished career.
reviews.author: Tom Meek

reviews.text: Tár is about power, guilt and the always tantalizing question of whether the art can or should absolve the artist for being who she is.
reviews.author: John Anderson

reviews.text: Highlights the flaws inherent to humanity — inherent to even the best of us, while also asking with a heavy hand by what metric “the best of us” can even be quantified.
reviews.author: Dan Scully

reviews.text: Tár’s fall from grace could lead to some overwrought melodrama with a lesser filmmaker. Instead, Field evokes that sensation of things getting from your control, never quite to be the same again.
reviews.author: Alci Rengifo

reviews.text: As a piece of storytelling ... Field's film is slightly more than an examination of power with some blatant, if drolly amusing, lesson-making...
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: Tár is something new, an insightful, mordantly funny look at power and the state of culture today.
reviews.author: Oscar Goff

reviews.text: An elegant musical backstage character study that follows the rise and fall of an egotistical world-famous female conductor.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: The anchor of this gorgeously photographed, impeccably acted triumph is Blanchett, and she is both mesmerizing and galvanizing.
reviews.author: Randy Myers

reviews.text: Riveting from start to finish, and energized by Blanchett’s stupendous performance, a fantastic score, crisp cinematography, and Field’s total command of tone, “TÁR” is an absolute triumph.
reviews.author: Gary M. Kramer

reviews.text: Less a movie than a seductive deep dive into an unraveling psyche of a woman who’s simultaneously defined by and apart from the world she has so confidently by the tail.
reviews.author: Ann Hornaday

reviews.text: Blanchett does it all here: Speaks three languages, plays piano, conducts with what looks to my untrained eye to be pretty fair stick technique, and changes the temperature in any given room Lydia enters with a glance.
reviews.author: Michael Phillips

reviews.text: Blanchett’s performance doesn’t suffice: she incarnates each moment sharply and emphatically but, despite her supremely skillful exertions, Field doesn’t forge dramatic unity.
reviews.author: Richard Brody

reviews.text: There is a lot swirling through the dense dialog and drama, as writer-director Todd Field comments on how personal actions and public reactions combine in a toxic brew in the social media age. And Cate Blanchett delivers a jaw-dropping performance.
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: There are many movies of the moment, but few are as fearlessly provocative as TÁR. We are Cate Blanchett’s orchestra, and her hold over us is infinite
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: Todd Field and Cate Blanchett team up for a story about a brilliant, flawed character.
reviews.author: Karen Gordon

reviews.text: In a masochistic way, a Blanchett character usually demands to be broken.
reviews.author: Josh Larsen

reviews.text: There’s nothing didactic about ‘Tár,’ nor any simple moral you can hashtag or put on a bumper sticker. The film is complicated. Difficult. Much like its protagonist.
reviews.author: Sean Burns

reviews.text: Field gave himself an imposing challenge for a comeback, and it’s one that, with the help of a career best Cate Blanchett, he is able to guide to something close to perfection.
reviews.author: Travis Hopson

reviews.text: Blanchett is absolutely tremendous and her performance is the reason to see it.
reviews.author: Rachel Wagner

reviews.text: Through a stunning performance by Cate Blanchett, Todd Field tells a story about modern culture, and what happens when a cult of personality starts to crack.
reviews.author: Adam Nayman

reviews.text: Blanchett is so convincing, and Field’s approach is so authentic, that it feels like an event, not just a movie.
reviews.author: G. Allen Johnson

reviews.text: Cate Blanchett has long been one of our greatest actresses but her latest performance is in a category all its own, an astonishing study of an artist so revered her genius has cast her bad behavior in shadow.
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: You will leave the theatre with questions, arguments, demands – but most of all a supremely fulfilling sense of satisfaction.
reviews.author: Barry Hertz

reviews.text: There is no doubt that Blanchett has given the performance of a lifetime. I was exhausted just reading all about her feats in the production notes.
reviews.author: Jeanne Kaplan

reviews.text: One could never accuse Cate Blanchett of being lazy. The result is a career best performance that should place her among the nominees for Best Actress in 2023.
reviews.author: David Kaplan

reviews.text: There’s never a dull moment with Ms. Blanchett’s measured performance to keep you focused. It’s impressive to a point, but too many loose ends deny the star a rational thread to hang onto.
reviews.author: Rex Reed

reviews.text: A gripping character study anchored by an astonishing turn from Blanchett.
reviews.author: Erica Abeel

reviews.text: Both harrowing and masterful — as art often is.
reviews.author: Bill Goodykoontz

reviews.text: Perhaps the best thing that can be said about Tár is that it is far more than a mere vehicle for one showboating performance. And even if it were, with a performance like this, who would mind?
reviews.author: K. Austin Collins

reviews.text: Each one of Field’s previous two films have been heralded as career-bests for him, and Tár is no exception. Field has only further honed his skills to deliver one of 2022’s best films that will no doubt dominate awards season.
reviews.author: Rachel West

reviews.text: That challenge, whether offered by Todd Field or any other filmmaker, is when cinema is at its best for me. That, or when it is just great relentless entertainment. These experiences are when cinema is an immeasurable gift.
reviews.author: David Poland

reviews.text: Cate Blanchett's riveting performance in writer/director Todd Field's TÁR makes it a psychological minefield of a drama. It's an absorbing portrait of someone intoxicated by her own power and facing a reckoning that's as unwelcome as a nasty hangover.
reviews.author: Carla Hay

reviews.text: 16 years was far too long to wait for Field’s next feature, but it’s finally here, and it’s great.
reviews.author: Matthew Dougherty

reviews.text: A mesmerizing psychological study of a tyrant's downfall. Cate Blanchett gives a spellbinding note-perfect performance. Expect many Oscar nominations.
reviews.author: Avi Offer

reviews.text: Tár is one of those rare films about a specific art that just about anyone watching it can embrace, even if they have no connection or previous knowledge of the art itself beyond a vague familiarity.
reviews.author: Jon Negroni

reviews.text: A remarkable portrait of a maestro under fire.
reviews.author: Rendy Jones

reviews.text: Tár is mesmerizing. Cate Blanchett's masterful performance captivates the screen for nearly three hours.
reviews.author: Maxwell Rabb

reviews.text: Blanchett’s love of control mirrors Lydia’s and in doing so, allows Blanchett to let go.
reviews.author: Carrie Wittmer

reviews.text: It’s a jagged, uncomfortable masterpiece.
reviews.author: Esther Zuckerman

reviews.text: Tár is a movie that defies easy judgments and prompts conversation. Remember when more movies did that?
reviews.author: Taylor Antrim

reviews.text: The match of larger-than-life actress to larger-than-life role is perfection.
reviews.author: Johnny Oleksinski

reviews.text: One of the best movies of the 21st century. While it may go unappreciated in our time, years from now this will stand the test of time.
reviews.author: Chris Bumbray

reviews.text: A tightly wound masterpiece that slices through class anxiety and power.
reviews.author: Alissa Wilkinson

reviews.text: TÁR dares us to think and listen intently in a world filled with so many distracting noises. For some this will be a welcomed task, for others it may be a grueling process during the movie’s two hours and thirty-eight minutes runtime.
reviews.author: Chauncey K. Robinson

reviews.text: TÁR is a richly detailed portrait of power and creative genius, led by Cate Blanchett’s towering performance.
reviews.author: Siddhant Adlakha

reviews.text: This is a #MeToo story told from the point of view of the powerful predator. If the main character was a man, audiences might not want to sit with the character for nearly three hours.
reviews.author: Tara McNamara

reviews.text: TÁR’s engrossing spell starts to dissipate over its final third, and yet this is that rare film about a creative person that feels neither self-pitying nor self-aggrandising.
reviews.author: Tim Grierson

reviews.text: TÁR is a singular piece of filmmaking that will go down as one of the greatest character studies of this era.
reviews.author: Prabhjot Bains

reviews.text: Start engraving the name Cate Blanchett on the Oscar for Best Actress. As a virtuoso  classical music conductor blindsided by cancel culture, she is an absolute stunner in a Todd Field spellbinder that belongs on every list of the best movies of 2022.
reviews.author: Peter Travers

reviews.text: Playing a formidable maestro, [Blanchett] proves herself one as well.
reviews.author: Nick Schager

reviews.text: [Cate Blanchett] seems to be working for herself, rather than to engage the audience, to make us either love her or hate her. Instead we observe how hard she works. It must be exhausting to perform this way. It’s certainly exhausting to watch.
reviews.author: Kyle Smith

reviews.text: Tár is an active conversation: compelling, fascinating, exhausting, and exhilarating, like a good jam session--like that first weekend in a new romance doomed to flameout but invigorating for a while. Not just great, Tár is important.
reviews.author: Walter Chaw

reviews.text: The adjectives that come to mind to describe Tár apply also to its protagonist: Todd Field’s third film is magisterial, enigmatic, self-contradictory, and wickedly seductive.
reviews.author: Dana Stevens

reviews.text: It’s a total knockout, both austere and dryly hilarious, and its quality is impossible to consider separately from its colossal lead performance.
reviews.author: Alison Willmore

reviews.text: Field has really achieved something remarkable with Tár. It’s one of those big character-driven films that is rare to be made nowadays. With its mesmerizing closeups and Blanchett’s commanding performance, the film is spectacular.
reviews.author: Dustin Chang

reviews.text: Tár has intellectual heft, and watching her deploy it is breathtaking. Blanchett pours equal parts charisma and intimidation into her career-best performance.
reviews.author: David Sims

reviews.text: Blanchett gives a colossal tour-de-force performance that may be the finest of her career... The answers Fields supplies are not always satisfying, but for much of the film, he and Blanchett orchestrate a mesmerizing character study.
reviews.author: Jake Coyle

reviews.text: [Field] moves smoothly from dry backstage comedy to something like gothic horror.
reviews.author: A.O. Scott

reviews.text: Not only does Blanchett’s command of the screen seem effortless, but she is able to synthesize the various sides of Lydia into a meaningful whole
reviews.author: Ryan Silberstein

reviews.text: From its very first moments, Tár announces itself as an event. It’s not just another movie—it’s an immersive visual and aural experience.
reviews.author: Murtada Elfadl

reviews.text: Like its protagonist, Tár is many things all at once: a psychological drama, a foray into horror, a (very) dry comedy, and a relationship drama.
reviews.author: Belen Edwards

reviews.text: I can’t fathom that Tár is a fictional character she feels so real. Like I could open Wikipedia and go on a bender through her early life, personal life (“Tár is openly gay”), and controversies section. It’s what makes TÁR one of the year’s greatest
reviews.author: Karl Delossantos

reviews.text: There have been 23 perfect games in MLB history, and Cate Blanchett delivers her perfect cinematic game in Todd Field’s TÁR. A hypnotic and fascinating deconstruction of a power-hungry and egotistical icon.
reviews.author: David Gonzalez

reviews.text: Field peels Lydia back like an onion, layer by layer, so that by the time we get to the last hour — and all hell breaks loose — we are experts about her world.
reviews.author: Roger Friedman

reviews.text: It’s hard to deny that Todd Field’s Tár, featuring what might very well come to be known as the already-two-time Oscar-winner Cate Blanchett’s definitive performance, is a powerhouse from top to bottom.
reviews.author: Jason Adams

reviews.text: Todd Field’s elegant and compelling drama is an of the moment look at power and its abuse. It’s a great, relevant piece of writing, brought to unshakeable life by a terrific cast, led by the inimitable Cate Blanchett.
reviews.author: Joanna Langfield

reviews.text: TÁR is an all-encompassing cinematic experience that's utterly engrossing and symbolically monumental.
reviews.author: Jeff Nelson

reviews.text: TÁR is that rarest of items: a prestige awards contender that’s also a genuine art film.
reviews.author: Glenn Kenny

reviews.text: Words of praise will be heaped upon Cate Blanchett, who delivers a nuanced performance for the ages. Her acute, wild physical gestures as she’s leading a masterclass or rehearsing a piece make it seem like she is performing her own style of choreography.
reviews.author: Sophia Ciminello

reviews.text: Begins from an adversarial place, as if challenging the audience to endure it. The film ultimately rewards its audience, but makes them work for it.
reviews.author: Fred Topel

reviews.text: Blanchett responds with perfect pitch. Her eyes are like spies, missing nothing, and her smile is a charmer’s knife.
reviews.author: Anthony Lane

reviews.text: The film is consistently compelling visually and aurally, but neither Todd Field nor Cate Blanchett seem quite decided on whether Tár’s comeuppance is a grand tragedy or a cosmic joke.
reviews.author: Keith Uhlich

reviews.text: A singularly strange offering...
reviews.author: Jonathan Romney

reviews.text: The social provocations are ultimately secondary leitmotifs in a work that strives first to make a fully rounded and fully angled fictional character from wisps of influence. They do, it seems, still make them like this.
reviews.author: Donald Clarke

reviews.text: Tár is a prime example of emotionally varied and exhilarating dramatic filmmaking at its finest.
reviews.author: Wilson Kwong

reviews.text: A stunning Cate Blanchett reaches new heights in this character study of worldwide success in the cancel-culture era.
reviews.author: J. Don Birnam

reviews.text: A film of rare elegance and sophistication.
reviews.author: Tomris Laffly

reviews.text: The movie belongs to Blanchett, in a turn so exacting and enormous that it feels less like a performance than a full-body possession.
reviews.author: Leah Greenblatt

reviews.text: Tár returns Todd Field's precise vision to screens, with an impeccable Cate Blanchett, to boot.
reviews.author: Joey Magidson

reviews.text: I didn’t want it to end.
reviews.author: Justin Chang

reviews.text: Blanchett... [turns] the movie from a moderately interesting and topical one into something quite beautiful.
reviews.author: Bilge Ebiri

reviews.text: Clearly, Lydia Tár is an absolute monster of a role, and Blanchett is utterly triumphant in it.
reviews.author: Tom O'Brien

reviews.text: The movie makes no excuses for Lydia’s behavior, and Blanchett’s performance faces it squarely.
reviews.author: Stephanie Zacharek

reviews.text: A rare film that dips its toe into the shark-infested waters of a woman's identity politics in a way that recognizes its complex shades of grey. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ruben Peralta Rigaud

reviews.text: There’s no kitsch, no promise of closure, no redemption arc. From the writer/director to the performers and technicians, everyone was on the same page to tell a story without sentimentality.
reviews.author: Zhuo-Ning Su

reviews.text: This is Cate Blanchett’s best performance since Carol, and it might be her best performance thus far...
reviews.author: Lex Briscuso

reviews.text: Overwhelming. {Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Mariona Borrull

reviews.text: For the most part, even at its excessive length, this is a tremendously absorbing film, for which everyone involved should take a bow, the remarkable Blanchett most of all.
reviews.author: Brian Viner

reviews.text: What is definitive, though, is just how greatly Tár succeeds in confronting its audience with a prescient issue: how fame and concentrated power beget maniacal and violent creatures.
reviews.author: Douglas Greenwood

reviews.text: Works more as psychological portrait than narrative freighter, putting you in the room with (and in the head of) a professional control freak as her life spirals out of control, all while observing the fallout with eerie calm.
reviews.author: Ben Croll

reviews.text: Cate Blanchett is captivating as formidable, world famous classical composer in Todd Fields’ frustrating study of the cult of genius.
reviews.author: Hannah Strong

reviews.text: Blanchett’s exacting iconoclast simply cannot be managed. It makes for a wild ride.
reviews.author: Adam Solomons

reviews.text: Recalling the likes of All About Eve and Amadeus, TÁR asks pertinent questions about cancel culture, artistic integrity and gender, while also providing a primer on orchestral politics and musical history.
reviews.author: Jane Crowther

reviews.text: The film wields its intelligence and style with total effortlessness, and its every move holds your gaze like a baton’s quivering tip.
reviews.author: Robbie Collin

reviews.text: A significant leap in maturity, control and confidence that takes risks at every step. What’s more, they consistently pay off in a transfixing movie that feels like no other.
reviews.author: David Rooney

reviews.text: A great reminder of what grown-up, middlebrow filmmaking, given the right blend of confidence and nurturing, can do—a work that, unlike its protagonist, refuses to talk down to you.
reviews.author: Rory O'Connor

reviews.text: TÁR is breathtaking entertainment, beautifully tailored in luxe, eerie Euro sleekness... That fine craftsmanship is all anchored by Blanchett’s alternately measured and ferocious performance.
reviews.author: Richard Lawson

reviews.text: Truly one of the most dazzling characterizations ever committed to film, whatever the gender categorization, Blanchett is spellbinding as a narcissistic orchestra conductor whose pride reaches the veritable heavens before leading her to ruin.
reviews.author: Nicholas Bell

reviews.text: One of the boldest and most exciting new American movies I’ve seen in years.
reviews.author: David Ehrlich

reviews.text: [Todd Fields] plays it icy cool, shooting Berlin in elegantly muted tones and orchestrating his drama with a surgical precision worthy of peak Michael Haneke.
reviews.author: Raphael Abraham

reviews.text: The film represents a daring and quite comprehensive immersion in a rarified world and features a lead performance the likes of which doesn’t come along very often.
reviews.author: Todd McCarthy

reviews.text: Todd Field’s Tár is a searing star vehicle for Cate Blanchett, gifting the actor with a fascinating, thorny character to bloodily untwine across an airy 158-minute runtime.
reviews.author: Steph Green

reviews.text: A timeless piece about the corrupting essence of power, exploitation, and the burdensome nature of the crown, elevated by a hydrogen bomb of a performance from Cate Blanchett.
reviews.author: Jack King

reviews.text: Of course, TÁR sinks or swims depending on the performances and Blanchett commands every one of these 158 minutes. She is already a generational performer but TÁR has to be one of her all-time best performances.
reviews.author: Brian Formo

reviews.text: [Blanchett's] performance will pierce you like a conductor’s baton through the heart...
reviews.author: Peter Bradshaw

reviews.text: TÁR is a Cate Blanchett masterclass.
reviews.author: Marshall Shaffer

synopsis: From writer-producer-director Todd Field comes TÁR, starring Cate Blanchett as Lydia Tár, the groundbreaking conductor of a major German Orchestra. We meet Tár at the height of her career, as she's preparing both a book launch and much-anticipated live performance of Mahler's Fifth Symphony. Over the ensuing weeks her life begins to unravel in a singularly modern way. The result is a searing examination of power, and its impact and durability in today's society.
